newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea ruling party rules out labour law revision.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea ruling party rules out labour law revision.

text.p: South Korea's ruling party chairman on Thrusday expressed regret over the railroading of a controversial labour law that sparked three weeks of strikes but ruled out its revision.
Chairman Lee Hong-koo told a news conference he was convinced the new law, which allows companies to lay off workers, was "an inevitable choice for an economic recovery and a new leap forward".
"Therefore I would like to make it clear that our party has no intention to revise the labour law at this point," he said.
Lee said he regretted opposition parties did not agree to introduce the new law, which was rammed through parliament on December 26 in a dawn session when opposition deputies were asleep.
Lee offered again to hold a televised debate with union leaders for "a right judgement by the people" and called on the opposition to begin dialogue to avert the crisis stemming from wildcat strikes.
